A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Feature Resemblance study. Their main text, equations, tables, figure, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching content across appendix and table renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-data experiments, natural-language fine-tuning results, curriculum and identity-bridge comparisons, and appendix analyses of feature alignment.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds Qwen-3-8B results and an activation-based feature diagnostic in Section 8.2 and Table 3.

M1.justification: The attention/value block, linear feature layer, cross-entropy training, curricula, and identity-bridge construction remain. Renaming the linear MLP and correcting cumulative training-time indices reconcile descriptions with the existing theoretical procedure; they do not establish a different core method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic analogy/two-hop tasks, generated natural-language entity-category dataset, and orthogonal-input depth experiment. Qwen-3-8B extends model scale on retained coverage; renaming the natural-language experiment does not introduce a new dataset or task.

E2.justification: The joint-training, similarity-first, attribution-first, and identity-bridge controls remain in their corresponding experiments. Qwen-3-8B is an additional architecture tested under the existing curricula, rather than a newly evaluated competing reasoning method.

E3.justification: v3 introduces an 8B model configuration and a feature diagnostic retaining the top 20% of MLP activations at relational tokens. Earlier experimental settings are otherwise retained; the newly stated natural-language fine-tuning hyperparameters do not establish that earlier settings changed.

E4.justification: Section 8.2 adds a Qwen-3-8B diagnostic examining whether shared representation components obscure feature alignment, reporting weak separation with full representations and using filtered activations. Existing end-to-end/ReLU, premise-frequency, and layer-depth analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations for synthetic experiments and point estimates for natural-language results. v3 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports Qwen-3-8B feature similarity/success of 0.3785/84% for joint training, 0.3757/75% for late attribution, and 0.2704/34% for late similarity. Existing main and appendix numerical results and Figure 1 are retained. These are additional-model results, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The supporting mathematics is substantially revised. Theorem 6 replaces the 0.8 alignment lower bound with Omega(1), while Section 7 makes random orthonormal inputs independent of labels explicit. Its appendix proof revises Lemma 18, stage indexing, error bounds, and the previously omitted input residual. Other appendices restore missing representation-decomposition terms, revise the joint-training alignment bound, and replace the no-alignment derivations for Propositions 8 and 9 with inner-product bounds.

C1.justification: The three principal contributions remain, but the abstract, introduction, and conclusion explicitly scope the guarantees to a minimal stylized model and describe larger-model evidence as qualitative agreement. The claimed empirical reach extends from 1.5B to 8B parameters.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly states that the short-prompt construction abstracts away discourse, positional structure, and long-range dependencies, and positions deep linear networks as a limited illustration. It changes the depth interpretation from monotonic increase to approximate non-decrease and adds an explanation involving task-irrelevant shared components for Qwen-3-8B's weak raw feature separation.

D1.justification: Unlike v1 Appendix N.2, v3 Appendix O.2 specifies 10 fine-tuning epochs, per-device batch size 16, learning rate 1e-5, zero weight decay, and FP16 training. Section 8.2 also specifies the 20% activation-retention diagnostic. Existing synthetic hyperparameters are unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds focused deep-linear-network context in Appendix A, citing Saxe, Kawaguchi, Laurent and Brecht, Hardt and Ma, and two Arora papers. It also connects the analogy definition to Gentner's structure-mapping theory and refines the comparison with Huang et al.; the central research positioning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introductory framing, model description, experimental narrative, conclusion, and impact statement undergo substantial rewriting. Terminology is standardized around a minimal transformer-style block and feature layer, and a proof roadmap organizes the appendix arguments. Citation style, headings, and front matter also change.

P2.justification: v3 adds the compact Qwen-3-8B Table 3, corrects Table 1's two-hop success column from A to R, and fixes the one-layer-only appendix table caption. The unchanged Figure 1 moves beside its discussion. Existing table structures and plot design are largely preserved despite document reflow.

improvement.justification: The decisive gain is improved mathematical consistency in this theory-centered paper: v3 replaces problematic no-alignment derivations, restores omitted representation terms, and revises the deep-linear proof and its overly specific 0.8 guarantee. Narrower assumptions and claims trade breadth for better alignment between statements and supporting arguments. The proof roadmap and disclosed fine-tuning settings further improve assessability. The added 8B experiment remains limited by filtered feature measurements and point estimates; it is supplementary to the substantial theoretical corrections.
